venue.name: Cumberland Museum and Archives
venue.description: The Cumberland Museum and Archives tells the story of the people of the former coal mining village of Cumberland, in the Comox Valley. Its exhibitions cover resource extraction, labour activism, immigration and community life in 20th century British Columbia. School programs run inside the museum and at nearby historic sites, including the No. 1 Japanese Townsite and the Chinatown site. The museum is open Tuesday to Sunday and closed on statutory holidays.
venue.hours_notes: Tuesday to Sunday, 11 AM to 4:30 PM. Closed on statutory holidays.

programs.name: Self-Guided Museum Exploration | Grades 3-12
programs.description: A self guided visit to the exhibitions using the museum's object based learning activity sheets. The museum describes the time frame as flexible. Booked through the school program form, which allows up to 30 people per booking, Wednesday to Friday, starting at 9:30, 11:00 or 1:00.
programs.what_children_do: Move through the exhibition rooms at their own pace with an activity sheet, stopping at whichever objects catch their eye.
programs.our_note: No guide comes with this one, so the adults in your group do the talking. It suits a class that is already comfortable looking at things quietly indoors.
programs.practical_summary: Indoors, and how long you stay is up to you. Washrooms, somewhere to eat and step free access are not described anywhere on the site, so ask when you book.

programs.name: No. 1 Japanese town Story Walk | Grades 4-12
programs.description: A guided outdoor walk of the No. 1 Japanese Townsite about the Japanese Canadian families who lived there. Groups meet at the No. 1 Japanese Townsite parking lot, not at the museum. The museum suggests bringing discs for the disc golf course afterwards, and asks groups to come dressed for the weather.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the old townsite with a guide for about three quarters of an hour, hearing what daily life, friendships and hardships were like for the families who lived there.
programs.our_note: You meet at the townsite car park rather than at the museum, so build the extra drive into the day. The whole thing is outdoors, so dress the group for rain.
programs.practical_summary: Outdoors from start to finish, with a car park to meet at. Washrooms, somewhere to eat and a wet weather plan are not mentioned, so worth a call.

programs.name: Cumberland Chinatown Story Walk | Grades 4-12
programs.description: A guided outdoor walk of the site of Cumberland's historic Chinatown, about the Chinese Canadian families who lived and worked there. Groups meet at Wong Gong (Jumbo's) Cabin, not at the museum, and there is a larger car park at the Coal Creek historic site nearby. The museum asks groups to come dressed for the weather.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the pathways of the old Chinatown site with a guide for about three quarters of an hour, picturing the businesses, music and cooking that once filled it.
programs.our_note: This one starts at a cabin off Comox Lake Road rather than at the museum, so check the meeting point the night before. It is outdoors the whole time.
programs.practical_summary: Outdoors from start to finish, with parking at the meeting point. Washrooms, somewhere to eat and a wet weather plan are not mentioned, so worth a call.

programs.name: Black Damp Fire Damp: No.6 Mine Play | Grades K-5
programs.description: A site specific outdoor program on the ground above the No. 6 Mine tunnels, with stories and audio interviews of Cumberland miners. The museum says the program can be adapted to suit the capacity and accessibility needs of your group, and that it is weather dependent. There is a playground and there are picnic tables at No. 6 Mine Park for afterwards.
programs.what_children_do: Crawl, run and collect pretend coal on the ground above the old mine tunnels, stopping to listen to recordings of miners talking about the work.
programs.our_note: This is the most physical thing they run and the only one written for the youngest grades outdoors. They say it can be adapted to what your group can manage, which is worth raising when you book.
programs.practical_summary: Outdoors and weather dependent, with a playground and picnic tables at the same park. Washrooms and a wet weather plan are not stated, so ask.

programs.name: Stolen Bases Guided Tour | Grades 5-12
programs.description: An hour long guided tour of the featured exhibition Stolen Bases, about local Japanese Canadian families in Cumberland. The museum says the tour includes discussion of the forced uprooting, incarceration, internment and dispossession of Japanese Canadians. The exhibition itself is listed as running from 23 March 2026 to 1 February 2027.
programs.what_children_do: Follow a guide through the exhibition for an hour, looking at objects and photographs and talking about what happened to Japanese Canadian families here.
programs.our_note: The subject matter is heavy and the museum says so plainly, so it lands better with a class that has already met it. It hangs on a temporary exhibition that is listed as closing in early February 2027.
programs.practical_summary: Indoors for the full hour. Washrooms, somewhere to eat and step free access are not described on the site, so ask when you book.

programs.name: Junior Historians Guided Exploration | Grades K-5
programs.description: A guided object handling session with the museum's education team. Children investigate everyday items with their senses and connect them to storytelling objects in the collection. The museum's own program page says Grades K to 5 while the school booking form lists this program as Grades K to 3.
programs.what_children_do: Handle everyday objects and use their senses to work out what each one was for, then hear the stories behind the matching pieces in the collection.
programs.our_note: This is the indoor option written for the youngest grades, so it is the easiest of theirs to sit through. Say the grade you are bringing when you book, because their pages do not agree on how far up it runs.
programs.practical_summary: Indoors and about three quarters of an hour. Washrooms, somewhere to eat and step free access are not stated on the site.

programs.name: Combination Tour Program
programs.description: Two of the museum's school programs run back to back on the same day. The museum offers this for groups larger than 30 participants, and says it suits combined classes, school groups and camps. You choose the two programs on the school booking form.
programs.what_children_do: Do two of the museum's programs in one day instead of one, so the day can mix object handling indoors with a walk outside.
programs.our_note: This is how they take a group over 30, so two classes travelling together fit here. Decide which two programs you want before you start the form.
programs.practical_summary: A full day, and how much of it is indoors depends on the two programs you pick. Washrooms and somewhere to eat are not described on the site.
programs.evidence: We can accommodate groups larger than 30 participants through our Combination Tour Program.

programs.name: Private Group Tour
programs.description: A private guided tour of the museum booked through a separate form, for groups that are not booking a school program. The museum says there is no size limit for indoor private tours and that a tour can be arranged for an individual or a larger group. The form asks for an estimated group size so the program can be designed around it, and it offers start times of 10 am, 11 am, 1 pm and 2 pm. No price is published.
programs.our_note: This is the route for a group that does not fit the school programs, a daycare for instance, since those are written from Kindergarten up. Nothing about the price is published, so ask what it costs when you send the form.
programs.practical_summary: Indoors, with no limit on group size stated. The price, how long it runs and what is on site are all things to ask about.
programs.evidence: There is no size limited for indoor private tours and can be arranged for the individual or larger group.

images.alt: A long wooden cabinet with a row of brass handled drawers above panelled doors, lit against a dark background.
A white gallery wall printed with a welcome text panel in large type, beside a white door frame.
A child sits on an old wooden mine cart in a museum corridor, facing a large wall image of forest and sky.
A woman holding a large green leaf stands behind an angled outdoor interpretive panel, with dense green forest behind her.

gaps: Price: no year or season is printed beside any of the program fees, so there is no way to tell from the site how current $2, $6 and $10 per student are. The school programs page was last changed in December 2025 and the program pages in January and April 2026.

Youngest age: the museum publishes grades, never ages. Every school program starts at Kindergarten and the booking form's grade list has no preschool option, so whether a daycare group can be taken is unanswered. The separate private group tour form is the likely route and says nothing about age.
Price for a private group tour is not published at all.

Capacity: 30 per booking is stated on the school booking form rather than on the program pages, and it is the school programs it applies to. The combination tour is for groups larger than 30 but no upper limit is given.
Lead time: no minimum notice is published. The booking form only says requests are reviewed between Wednesday and Friday.
Lunch space: nothing on the site about eating indoors at the museum. Picnic tables are mentioned at No. 6 Mine Park, which is where the mine play program runs, not at the museum.
Washrooms: not mentioned anywhere on the site.
Rain backup: not mentioned. Three of the six programs are outdoors and two of those say to come dressed for the weather.
Accessibility, stroller access and bus parking are not addressed. Only the mine play program says it can be adapted to a group's accessibility needs.
How many adults have to come is not stated, and nothing says whether accompanying adults pay.
Deposit, when payment is due and what happens if you cancel are not published.

RETRIEVAL NOTE: three of the six program pages on this site (the mine play, the Stolen Bases tour and Junior Historians) return an empty body to a plain fetch and only render in a browser. A fetch-only re-run will appear to find those programs missing.

Coordinates: the map on the visit page is a Google Maps embed carrying only a map viewport centre, not a place pin, and the contact page embed is a plain place-name search. The coordinates recorded here were geocoded from the street address on the contact page, and they land about 180 m from where that map is centred.
Images: none of the photographs on this site carry alt text, so all four alt lines here were written after opening each image and looking at it.
The Stolen Bases guided tour hangs on a temporary exhibition. The exhibitions page dates that show 23 March 2026 to 1 February 2027, so this program should be re-checked before the 2027 spring term.

conflicts.note: Their pages give two different top grades for the Junior Historians session. The program page says up to grade 5, the booking form's own list says up to grade 3. If you are bringing a grade 4 or 5 class, say so when you book.
